title: Policy-Based Routing: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Normally, routers decide by destination alone. What if you want to route by who sent the packet? That's policy based routing.

lines.t: What if you want something else?

scenes.heading: The VIP entrance
scenes.narration: Think of a concert with a special VIP entrance. A route map decides who counts as VIP, using match rules. The set command sends them down a different path. You apply it on the interface where packets come in. Everyone else goes through the normal door as usual.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. It doesn't change the routing table. Apply it on the incoming interface. And it can match on much more than destination.

items.wrong: PBR goes on the outbound side

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva policy-based routing lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. P B R routes by policy, not just destination. Use a route map with match and set. Apply it inbound. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva policy-based routing lab.
